posture_change_this_round.claim_withdrawn: Round 4's 'a case nobody anticipated fails closed'.
posture_change_this_round.why_it_was_false: None of the three round-5 phantoms is a shape violation -- each contains a syntactically perfect GitHub-markdown table. They are PROVENANCE failures: the text is a real grid that is not a reading of the page. No markdown predicate can see that, because by markdown the input is correct.
posture_change_this_round.test_renamed: test_the_predicate_fails_closed_on_a_shape_nobody_enumerated -> test_junk_carrying_pipes_is_refused. Seven junk inputs cannot establish a universal and the test no longer pretends to.
posture_change_this_round.new_framing: Documented in the predicate's own docstring as a deliberately CONSERVATIVE INTERIM, not a decision procedure. Operative rule: FAIL CLOSED. Refusing a real grid costs the marker, which is what ships today; accepting a phantom silently replaces a page with text describing nothing. Asymmetric costs, asymmetric predicate.
posture_change_this_round.sound_fix_pointer: #268 -- a geometry-corroborated fact recorded at extraction time, serving this caller AND flagged_model_page_output (#259), which has the same hole in merged code today.

three_findings.case: prose line with one pipe as header
three_findings.remedy_NOT_taken: The reviewer's proposed definition -- a header whose cells are 'not all separators and not all blank' -- does NOT close its own finding. Measured: ['noise','a'] is neither, so the phantom would have been ACCEPTED. Implementing it would have been the fifth confident wrong measurement.
three_findings.remedy_taken: Two fail-closed rules: (a) EXACTLY ONE separator row per block -- a doubled separator is ambiguous about where the table starts; (b) the header must share the separator's BORDER STYLE -- a table is emitted consistently by whatever wrote it, a sentence that happens to precede a separator is not. Leaves all-bordered and all-unbordered spellings alone.
_INDENTED_CODE blanks any line indented 4+ spaces or a tab, applied AFTER fence stripping because a fence's content may itself be indented.
_strip_html_comments runs FIRST (comments can contain fence markers); an unclosed '<!--' swallows the rest of the document, same fail-closed reasoning as an unclosed fence.

deliberate_tightenings_vs_round4.case: separator, separator, then a real body row
deliberate_tightenings_vs_round4.why: A block with more than one separator is ambiguous about where its table starts; under a fail-closed interim ambiguity costs the marker.

deliberate_tightenings_vs_round4.case: pipe-bearing prose directly above a grid
deliberate_tightenings_vs_round4.why: Removes round 4's offset scan -- the header is now the run's FIRST line, per review instruction. That flexibility was the room the prose-as-header phantom lived in. Cost is a marker on a real grid whose run opens with prose and no blank line; a blank line still separates runs, so a grid after a paragraph is unaffected.

my_own_expectation_corrected.case: header cell that is literally --- text (| --- | b |)
my_own_expectation_corrected.resolution: The predicate is right and I was wrong. The body is real content and there is exactly one separator; refusing it would reject legitimate tables. Corrected in the corpus with the reasoning rather than forcing the code to match a bad expectation.
